name: Waddell & Reed

summary.text: Waddell & Reed Financial was a Kansas-based mutual fund company. The September 30, 2010 joint SEC–CFTC staff report on the May 6, 2010 'flash crash' described a large automated sell programme by a mutual fund complex to sell 75,000 E-Mini S&P 500 futures contracts (about $4.1 billion) as a trigger of the afternoon's liquidity crisis; the report did not name the firm, but press reports identified it as Waddell & Reed, which said it had been managing downside risk in its portfolios.

sources.title: Findings Regarding the Market Events of May 6, 2010: Report of the Staffs of the CFTC and SEC to the Joint Advisory Committee on Emerging Regulatory Issues
Regulators Release Flash Crash Probe Report

facts.claim: The joint SEC–CFTC staff report of September 30, 2010 described a large, programmed effort by a mutual fund complex to sell 75,000 E-Mini futures contracts worth about $4.1 billion on May 6, 2010.
facts.quote: a large, programmed effort by a mutual fund complex to sell 75,000 E-Mini futures contracts, worth $4.1 billion

sources.title: Findings Regarding the Market Events of May 6, 2010
Regulators Release Flash Crash Probe Report

facts.claim: The report did not name the seller; press reports citing the Associated Press identified it as Waddell & Reed of Shawnee Mission, Kansas.

Waddell & Reed E-Mini Trades Said to Help Trigger May 6 Crash

facts.claim: A Waddell & Reed spokesman said the firm had merely been trying to manage downside risk in its portfolios.
facts.quote: We were merely trying to manage downside risk in our portfolios.

facts.claim: The joint report states that it reflects the findings of the CFTC and SEC staffs and that the Commissions expressed no view on its analysis, findings or conclusions.
facts.quote: The Commissions have expressed no view regarding the analysis, findings or conclusions contained herein.

sources.title: Findings Regarding the Market Events of May 6, 2010

facts.claim: Market data firm Nanex, which obtained raw data on the trade, challenged elements of the report's account of the sell programme.
facts.quote: some elements of this story have already been challenged by market research firm Nanex

sources.title: Regulators Release Flash Crash Probe Report

openQuestions: The site attributes the flash crash to high-frequency trading; the joint report attributes the trigger to the large sell programme interacting with HFT liquidity withdrawal, while Nanex disputed the emphasis. The 2015 CFTC/DOJ action against Navinder Sarao (already on the site) is a further strand.
Eric Hunsader of Nanex was not named in any source returned, so no file was written for him.
